Model: gpt-6.1-sol, high. Scope: granted claim 325 only, Process_CORD_Packet.

438 bytes, f5cb888dacdd8680831c1081a77a0e9af2e602037d9ad05a9c1de9f9fab4f1f3.
Header retention did not itself reopen this target.

## Independent observations

Actual retained3 baseline objdiff and all four prior distinct output groups
were inspected. Retail loads sender into EBP at 0x85A08E, before entering the
loop. At 0x85A0B1 it loads full session dword into EBX, calls ntohs on the packet
ID, and saves EAX to the dead sender parameter slot at 0x85A0BE. The compare at
0x85A0D3 uses only BX and that slot's low word. Native holds session in EBP and
ID in EBX and reloads sender, so this is a lifetime/allocation issue across
the entire loop, not merely a different byte-order conversion instruction.
The early ID/sender load splits changed scratch coloring but never this choice.

The loop's existing ArrayList::get (arraylist.h:623) returns false without
overwriting con when out of range. Retail likewise retains ESI on the failed
inline-get branch. Replacing this with getPointer, resetting con inside the
loop, or treating a failed get as a skip changes behavior. There is no
existing getter on CordCon for these fields. Inventing an accessor merely to
spend inline budget has no new source evidence here.

The unexamined warning argument is an actual __int64 Key_ member (+0x20/+0x24),
despite the existing format string saying %d. Retail +0x115/+0x118 loads both
halves into ECX/EAX, pushes both, then loads sender port into AX at +0x11D.
Native loads the port before the low-key push; the address-split context still
interleaves that port load. Retail later reads sender address after ntohs
returns and calls ntohl before Message_Warn. The success branch also reads
sender port after handlePacket and converts/stores it before breaking.
Neither warning values nor successful port load/conversion were named in any
of the twelve first-tier forms: their call-local hypothesis affected only
handlePacket(data,len). This is a concrete late actual-argument site, with
demonstrated workflow 3.1.2 named-argument and real-conversion mechanisms.

## Batch 1: full-width actual warning key local

key_base and key_address materialize precisely the existing __int64 key
argument immediately before the warning. The second uses the actual prior
17-row address-load form, rebased by target-only replacement. No conversion,
callback, failure branch, logger text/line, or successful Port_ store moves.
The key's two dword loads belong to the same existing evaluation before the
port conversion. This can affect late allocation/scheduling and thereby sender
priority; it is not a guarantee of matching and must be judged by actual code.

## Batch 2: remaining actual load/conversion sites, conditional on inspection

successport_address splits only the existing successful ntohs input/result
using the same typed local, on the best prior address-split context.
warning_address names key first, then port load/ntohs, then address load/ntohl,
then invokes the unchanged warning with those exact values and widths. This
preserves actual native call and member-read order and prevents introducing a
key read after conversions. all_real_splits combines these changes with the
two initial real splits, analogous to the actual coordinated ACK1 solve.
These are purposeful site/interaction tests, not permutations of equivalent
names, declarations or casts. Inspect batch 1 before deciding execution and
any rebasing or combining. Stop on three consecutive no-cut batches or when
no distinct evidence-backed lever remains. Eight batches would require the
repository checkpoint; changing models does not reset limits.

## Prior evidence and rejection boundaries

Original history contains three forms (int ID, ushort session, original
locals); exact sources are absent, so no fabricated replay is claimed.
First tier has twelve distinct source inputs, five batches and four actual
raw/masked output groups; all twelve replayed and both complete retained2
124-pair sets independently checked in sol/prior-audit.json. Original122 also
survive in each. The final three no-cut batches were ID scope, sender pointer
local and handlePacket argument locals across three contexts. They remain
duplicates and are not proposed again. Explain's combined-form field-offset
diagnosis aligns a high Key_ half with a low half; source field offsets are
unchanged and this is an instruction-alignment artifact, not a layout lead.

ACK1's audited five load/conversion splits, ACK2's ignored actual conversion
and pointer block before delete, and PumpConnections' five actual group tests
plus header-consumer proof were reviewed as real mechanisms. There is no new,
add-list, delete sequence in this function to which the latter pointer-lifetime
solution directly transfers. Native and retail both have the same profile
frame and only the sender/session/ID liveness provides a concrete opening.
No fake lifetime/storage, dead reads, arbitrary helper, header edit, flag sweep,
or hoisted field read is authorized by these examples.

All five generated inputs are currently UNCOMPILED. prepare.py verifies active
base hash, target-only edits, exact-byte replay and physical log/assert guard.
Each replay.json records before/after edits, full diff and hashes below 64 KiB.
No compiler state, production, header, snapshot, tracked metadata, commit or
